EMBA 准备阶段文件分析｜2026.6

核心判断：这组 PDF 属于 EMBA preparation stage，而不是正式课程笔记。

证据链：2026-06-05 offer of admission，2026-06-08 certificate of enrolment，随后进入 onboarding、课程日历、费用政策和选课战略。

行政侧：Maastricht EMBA On-Campus, part-time, academic year 2026/27；offer 与 enrolment 已形成正式状态。

执行侧：先完成 UM password、Microsoft Authenticator MFA、Canvas、UM email、Teams，并打开 General、Electives、On-campus 等 Teams channel notifications。

财务侧：on-campus track EUR 34,500，六期 instalments，每期 EUR 5,750；September/November start rhythm 对应 September、January、May、September、January、May；注意 30 天 payment term、late cancellation EUR 500、premature termination 25% remaining instalments。

课程侧：on-campus track 是 Leading in Learning、5 个 face-to-face core modules、3 个 face-to-face elective weeks、Leadership Development Trajectory、Business Research Methods、Business Consulting Project。Offer 与 programme outline 对 2026 年 9 月第一教学周结束日存在 9/12 vs 9/11 的差异，建议向 MBA office 确认。

选课侧：Digital Business、Responsible Leadership、Sustainable Innovation 三个方向各有三周；总共选三周，至少一周 Maastricht 附近，至少一周 abroad。对 Leo 来说，Digital Business 与 AI/product/company-building 高度相关，Responsible Leadership 与 founder/leadership growth 高度相关，Sustainable Innovation 更适合 impact/business-model redesign。

阅读侧：The Lost Art of Thinking in Large Organizations 提醒我，EMBA 不只是补框架，而是重建 strategic thinking muscle：保护思考时间、从具体 use case 开始、测试假设边界、通过 delegation 释放 thinking capacity。

months.reflection:
手写笔记整理｜2026-07-01 至 2026-07-03

这几页笔记的主线，是我对 leadership 的理解从“领导者要给出更好的答案”，转向“领导者要创造让别人更好思考、表达和学习的环境”。真正的领导力不是把大家留在舒适房间里，而是让人看见盲点、暂停自动反应、敢于表达不同意见，并把经验转化成可重复的学习。

1. Lead in Learning：从真实问题开始

EMBA 的学习不是收集框架，而是把真实工作中的个人挣扎、个人兴趣和现实情境带进课堂。Leadership question 应该来自 daily work 和 personal struggle。Coaching 的价值，是帮助我看见自己的 autopattern、assumption 和 habitual response。一个重要提醒是：不要只是让自己或别人舒服，而是 enable others to think differently。

2. Memory Making：从点到线，再到图像

Memory making 的练习提醒我：经验本身只是 points，反思把点连成 lines，最终我们才形成 picture。风险在于，我很容易把自己的 picture 当成事实。笔记里反复出现的句子是：what we hear is an opinion, not a fact；everything we see is a perspective, not the truth。所以 blind spot 不是羞耻，而是 input。反思、diary shadowing、appointment with myself，是把经验变成学习的机制。

3. Listening 与 Coaching：先理解，再回应

倾听不是等别人说完以后马上给建议，而是先让对方感到被理解、被信任。我的具体练习包括：wait until finish，不要太早 interrupt；先 summary and reflection，再进入 clarification；分享问题时，先 only listening；让 coachee 自己修复问题，而不是由 coach 提供答案。这里也出现了 three voices of judgment, cynicism, fear。它们提醒我，在真正听见别人之前，我常常已经开始评价、防御或害怕失控。

4. AI：放大能力，但不替代判断

AI 的位置不是替代人，而是提高准备、反思和表达的质量。笔记里的 60 -> 80 normal、80 -> 120 with AI，可以理解成：AI 应该帮助我把工作标准提高，而不是让人偷懒。使用 AI 时，人必须 in the lead。AI 可以做 summary、roleplay、pressure test、generate options，但最终判断、责任和学习仍然属于人。直接复制 generative content 不是 learning。

5. Organizational Learning：把个人洞察变成组织能力

学习不只发生在课堂。笔记里有 70/20/10：on-the-job learning、informal learning、formal learning。真正重要的是把个人经验通过 observe -> explain -> practice -> combine 变成团队语言和组织习惯。Nonaka and Takeuchi 的 knowledge-creating company 也提醒我：知识要有 home，要能被保存、分享、练习和再创造。组织学习不是一次 workshop，而是持续的 practice until it becomes second nature。

6. Inclusion & Diversity：让差异被看见、被听见、被转化

7 月 3 日的 Inclusion & Diversity 笔记，把 culture map、communication、country difference 和 storytelling 放在一起。多元不是口号，而是具体行为：我是否知道对方来自哪里、现在处在什么语境；我是否意识到不同文化对直接表达、反馈、权威、沉默和 disagreement 的理解不同；我是否能让不同视角进入讨论。好的表达也不是堆数据，而是 make it personal、keep it authentic、target the audience、create stickiness。

7. 我的行动清单

会前：写下我想要的 outcome，也写下我可能带入房间的 assumption。

会中：少打断，先总结，再回应；先听完事实、情绪和对方的解释；至少问一个能帮助别人 think differently 的问题。

会后：用三句话复盘：what happened；what did I make it mean；what else could be true。

使用 AI：让 AI 帮我找盲点、模拟不同利益相关者、整理事实和选项，但最后判断必须由我负责。

团队学习：把好的实践留下来，变成 shared language、meeting rhythm、checklist 或 story。领导力不是我一个人变强，而是让团队更会学习。
months.markdown:
# EMBA July 2026 Handwritten Notes Analysis

Source photos: IMG_6900 to IMG_6912  
Dates inferred from notes: 2026-07-01 to 2026-07-03  
Topic cluster: Lead in Learning, Memory Making, Listening/Coaching, AI, Organizational Learning, Inclusion & Diversity

## 1. One-Line Summary

This set of notes is less about "learning leadership theory" and more about practicing a different leadership posture: create safety, listen longer, surface blind spots, help people think differently, and use AI as a mirror or assistant rather than as a substitute for human judgment.

## 1A. Search Card

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Best month | 2026-07 |
| Best use | Answer questions about the first EMBA leadership-learning notes, coaching posture, listening, psychological safety, AI use, organizational learning, inclusion, and storytelling |
| Original source layer | Handwritten-note images IMG_6900 to IMG_6912 |
| Markdown layer | Searchable analysis and personal action plan |
| Core leadership shift | From giving sharper answers to creating better thinking conditions |
| Chinese aliases | 领导力, 倾听, 教练, 心理安全, 反思, AI, 组织学习, 包容 |

## 2. Main Thread

The notes move through three connected layers:

1. Personal leadership awareness: notice your automatic patterns, assumptions, emotional reactions, and comfort zone.
2. Interpersonal leadership practice: listen without interrupting, ask better questions, coach instead of giving answers, and help others feel understood.
3. Organizational learning: turn individual insights into shared learning through reflection, storytelling, documentation, AI-assisted preparation, and repeated practice.

The strongest sentence in the notes is probably: "Not make your comfortable room; enabling others to think differently." That captures the leadership idea underneath the whole class.

## 3. Notes By Date

### 2026-07-01 - Lead In Learning

Key raw points:

- Intro program, onboarding guidance, Canvas/UMIO/MU.
- Learning groups and coaching groups.
- Leadership questions should come from personal struggle, personal interest, and real daily work situations.
- Coaching: notice automatic patterns and assumptions.
- "Shifting perspective."
- "Not make your comfortable room."
- Leadership is about enabling others to think differently.

Analysis:

The first day seems designed to set up EMBA as a reflective practice environment, not just a content-delivery program. The important move is from "I attend class and collect frameworks" to "I bring real work tension into class, test it, and return with a changed way of seeing."

The coaching angle is especially important. The notes suggest that leadership development starts when you can observe your own autopilot: where you interrupt, where you defend, where you rush to advice, and where you assume your perspective is the full truth.

Personal application:

- Bring one real leadership tension to each module.
- Before asking "what is the answer?", ask "what assumption am I standing on?"
- Use coaching conversations to test patterns, not to seek reassurance.

### 2026-07-02 - Memory Making, Reflection, And Alumni Insights

Key raw points:

- "Alumni introduction."
- Bridge with scientist and corporate; MBA/PhD connection.
- "Memory making" with Professor Sonja.
- Connect points to lines to pictures, possibly "to a cat."
- Blind spot as input.
- Open my perspective.
- What we hear is an opinion, not a fact.
- Everything we see is a perspective, not the truth.
- Energized -> next? -> find what excited you; summary and do again.
- Diary shadowing; appointment with myself.

Analysis:

This day centers on how experience becomes memory, and how memory becomes learning. A useful interpretation:

- Points are isolated moments.
- Lines are patterns across moments.
- Pictures are the meaning we construct.

The risk is that leaders often confuse their "picture" with reality. The notes about opinion, perspective, and truth push against that. Reflection is not just journaling for emotion; it is a way to separate observation from interpretation.

Personal application:

- After important meetings, write three lines: What happened? What did I make it mean? What else could be true?
- Treat blind spots as data, not as shame.
- Keep an "appointment with myself" for weekly reflection.

### Listening And Coaching Practice

Key raw points:

- Share your expectation with child.
- Find the common area of misunderstanding.
- Understand the father's situation.
- Listen to others' feedback.
- No more distractions in the meeting.
- More focus, let others feel heard.
- Being understood / being trusted.
- "Summary and reflection."
- Share your problem to others.
- Only listening; no clarification questions at first.
- Let the coachee fix his problem, not provide solutions.
- Wait until finish; do not interact too early.
- Three voices of judgment: judgment, cynicism, fear.

Analysis:

The listening notes are very practical. They show a shift from "leader as solver" to "leader as container." A container leader does not disappear; they create the conditions for the other person to think.

The "three voices" are useful diagnostics:

- Judgment: "I already know if this is good or bad."
- Cynicism: "This will not work anyway."
- Fear: "If I open up, I may lose control or look weak."

These voices often appear before real listening begins. The note "wait until finish" is a small behavior with large impact. It gives the other person enough space to complete the thought before the leader shapes it.

Personal application:

- In coaching mode, start with listening only.
- Summarize before advising: "What I hear is..."
- Ask: "What have you already tried?" and "What would a good next step look like?"
- Avoid early clarification if it interrupts emotional flow.

### AI As Guide, Not Replacement

Key raw points:

- Define AI usage: 60 -> 80 normal, 80 -> 120 with AI.
- Do not let AI guide or generate all; human in the lead.
- Test how people master the knowledge.
- Use AI summary and business inputs.
- Content copy from generative content is not learning.
- Make sure knowledge and insight have a "home" in the organization.
- Build communities of practice.
- Be conscious about AI use.
- AI can help generate content and test / spark learning.

Analysis:

The AI notes are unusually mature. The class seems to be arguing for AI as a learning amplifier, not a shortcut. The key question is not "can AI produce the answer?" but "does AI help humans become better at thinking, practicing, and judging?"

The 60/80/120 line can be interpreted as a performance standard:

- 60: baseline human work.
- 80: solid human work.
- 120: AI-assisted work that raises the bar, but still requires human judgment.

Personal application:

- Use AI to prepare, roleplay, summarize, and pressure-test.
- Do not outsource the final judgment.
- Ask AI to reveal assumptions and missing perspectives.
- Save useful prompts as organizational learning assets.

Suggested prompts:

```text
Act as a skeptical EMBA coach. Help me identify the assumptions behind this leadership decision.
```

```text
Roleplay a colleague who disagrees with me. Ask me questions before giving advice.
```

```text
Summarize this meeting into facts, interpretations, emotions, decisions, and unresolved questions.
```

### Organizational Learning

Key raw points:

- Learning is the process; working is the result.
- 70/20/10: on the job, informal learning, formal learning.
- On-the-job learning around 70%.
- Informal learning around 20%.
- Formal learning around 10%.
- "Take the listener's perspective."
- Can the job learning be named? Nonaka and Takeuchi, 1994.
- Observe -> explain -> practice -> combine.
- Practice until it becomes second nature.
- Organization learning: tap a song, listen, communicate culture.
- Clean goals, clean framework, trust.

Analysis:

The organizational learning notes connect individual reflection to collective capability. The core pattern is:

1. Observe experience.
2. Explain what happened.
3. Practice a new behavior.
4. Combine insights with others.
5. Turn it into shared language, routines, and culture.

This is where leadership becomes scalable. A private insight is useful, but an organization changes when the insight becomes a habit, a meeting format, a checklist, a story, or a shared standard.

Personal application:

- Build a simple after-action review rhythm: What happened? Why? What did we learn? What will we change?
- Capture good practices in one shared place.
- Let teams create language for what they are learning.

### Inclusion & Diversity - 2026-07-03

Key raw points:

- "Inclusion & Diversity 7.3."
- Where you are from / where you currently belong.
- Communication.
- First feeling: autopilot.
- Second feeling: focus.
- The culture map; different forms.
- Country differences: animation, life, income, population.
- Data can be fun.
- Leadership is not possible without body support / resources.
- Make it personal, keep it authentic, wow factor, target audience, stickiness.
- Friendly speech: target audience, share information, practice presentation, eye contact and gesture.
- Storytelling: mirror -> picture the story; storytelling is interactive.

Analysis:

This section seems to combine cultural awareness with presentation practice. The "culture map" idea is useful because it reminds leaders that communication norms are not neutral. Directness, hierarchy, timing, silence, disagreement, and feedback all carry cultural meaning.

The presentation notes point to a practical rule: make the message personal and audience-specific. Data alone does not move people; data needs story, target audience, and emotional connection.

Personal application:

- Before speaking to an international group, map likely differences in communication, authority, and feedback style.
- Start with a human story, then show the data.
- Make one audience-specific point instead of trying to impress everyone.

## 4. Cross-Cutting Insights

### Insight 1: Leadership Starts With Self-Observation

Your notes repeatedly return to autopilot, assumptions, blind spots, judgment, cynicism, and fear. This suggests a leadership development model where self-awareness is not soft; it is operational. A leader who cannot observe their own reactions will unconsciously make the room smaller.

### Insight 2: The Leader's Job Is To Create A Better Thinking Environment

The notes do not define leadership as command. They define it as helping people think, speak, learn, and coordinate better. The leader shapes the space: safety, focus, trust, reflection, and standards.

### Insight 3: Learning Requires Repetition And Reflection

The line "summary and do again" matters. Learning is not the moment of insight; it is the loop after insight. The notes favor practice, reflection, feedback, and second nature.

### Insight 4: AI Raises The Standard Only When Humans Stay In The Lead

The notes are not anti-AI, but they are anti-laziness. AI is useful when it helps people prepare, compare, summarize, roleplay, and test. It is harmful when it replaces thinking, authorship, or accountability.

### Insight 5: Inclusion Is A Leadership Practice, Not A Slogan

Inclusion appears in the notes as listening, cultural mapping, communication, and making others feel understood. It is behavioral: who gets heard, who feels safe, whose perspective becomes visible, and how differences are translated into better collective work.

## 4A. Knowledge Map

| Cluster | Core idea | Work application |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Self-observation | Notice autopilot, assumptions, judgment, cynicism, fear, and blind spots | Before meetings, write the assumption I may be bringing into the room |
| Listening and coaching | Listen longer and help others repair or reframe their own problem | Summarize before responding and ask one better question |
| Psychological safety | Leadership creates conditions where people can speak, learn, and disagree productively | Make meetings safer without lowering standards |
| AI-assisted learning | AI should raise preparation, reflection, and pressure testing while humans stay accountable | Use AI to roleplay, summarize, and find blind spots, then decide myself |
| Organizational learning | Personal insight becomes valuable only when turned into shared routines or language | Convert one insight into a team checklist, story, or meeting rhythm |
| Inclusion and culture | Culture and difference appear in communication norms, authority, feedback, and belonging | Map audience differences before presenting or leading a mixed group |

## 5. Suggested Personal Action Plan

### Before Meetings

- Write the outcome I want.
- Write the assumption I may be bringing into the room.
- Decide whether I am in decision mode, listening mode, or coaching mode.

### During Meetings

- Do not interrupt too early.
- Summarize before responding.
- Ask at least one question that helps others think differently.
- Watch for the three voices: judgment, cynicism, fear.

### After Meetings

- Capture facts, interpretations, emotions, decisions, and open questions.
- Write one sentence on what I learned about myself.
- Write one sentence on what the team learned.

### Weekly EMBA Reflection

- What was the strongest blind spot this week?
- Where did I create safety?
- Where did I rush to solve?
- What did AI help me see, and what did I decide myself?
- What practice should I repeat next week?

## 6. Possible Cleaned-Up Reflection For July EMBA Page

July's first EMBA notes show a clear shift in my understanding of leadership. Leadership is not mainly about having sharper answers. It is about creating the conditions for better thinking: safety, trust, listening, reflection, and the courage to question assumptions. The strongest learning for me is to notice my autopilot, wait longer before responding, and help others find their own answers instead of rushing to provide solutions. AI can raise the standard of preparation and reflection, but only if human judgment remains in the lead. Inclusion and diversity also become practical through listening, cultural awareness, and communication that makes different perspectives visible.

## 7. Image Index

- `images/IMG_6900.jpeg` - Lead in Learning, 2026-07-01.
- `images/IMG_6901.jpeg` - Levels of listening / habits / outside-in perspective.
- `images/IMG_6902.jpeg` - Three voices of judgment, cynicism, fear.
- `images/IMG_6903.jpeg` - Listening, coaching, being understood and trusted.
- `images/IMG_6904.jpeg` - Alumni introduction, memory making, blind spots, reflection.
- `images/IMG_6905.jpeg` - Leadership, perspective, process, creativity, minority feeling.

- `images/IMG_6908.jpeg` - 70/20/10 learning and Nonaka/Takeuchi knowledge creation.

thinkingQuestions.title: 真实问题，才是学习入口
thinkingQuestions.position: 下半页，Lead in Learning 开场练习
thinkingQuestions.original: Q/A: 5min, personal strggle, personal interest / why we develop in leader role / situation in real daily work
thinkingQuestions.context: 课堂要求从 personal struggle、personal interest 和 real daily work 中提出 leadership question；旁边还有“1min and give answer”。
thinkingQuestions.reconstruction: 我不应该把 EMBA 变成框架收藏。每次学习都要从一个仍在发生的真实困境出发，说明它为什么与我的领导角色有关，再用课堂去重新定义问题和测试假设。只有问题回到现实行为和结果，学习才真正发生。
thinkingQuestions.evidenceBoundary: 原文清楚记录了课堂练习要求；“不做框架收藏”及完整学习闭环是 Codex 根据上下文补齐，需由 Leo 确认。
thinkingQuestions.reviewPrompt: 我现在最值得带进 EMBA 的一个 live leadership question 到底是什么？
thinkingQuestions.followUp: 补写一个具体事件：谁参与、发生了什么、我当时如何判断、为什么仍未解决。
thinkingQuestions.learningReflection: 下一个模块结束后检查：问题是否被重新定义，行为是否改变，而不只记录学了什么。

thinkingQuestions.title: 领导力要先看见自动模式，再帮助别人换一个角度
thinkingQuestions.original: Coaching -> auto pattern. be aware / "shifting perspective" of assumption / "Not make your comfortable room" / enabling others to think differently
thinkingQuestions.context: 在领导力问题练习之后，笔记转向 coaching、automatic pattern、assumption 和 perspective shifting。
thinkingQuestions.reconstruction: 领导者首先要觉察自己的自动反应和默认假设，否则所谓提问可能只是把别人带回自己的旧答案。Coaching 的价值不是维护一个让自己舒服的房间，而是创造足够的空间，让对方看见另一种解释并形成自己的判断。方向和边界仍要清楚，但不能抢走别人的思考权。
thinkingQuestions.evidenceBoundary: 前两句直接来自相邻原文；“方向和边界”来自 IMG_6907 的课堂记录，是跨页补充，不是本页原句。
thinkingQuestions.reviewPrompt: 我最近一次给建议时，是在帮助对方思考，还是在让局面更符合我的习惯？
thinkingQuestions.followUp: 选一次真实对话，写下自己的 auto pattern、assumption，以及一个可以替代旧反应的问题。
thinkingQuestions.learningReflection: 复盘对方最终是否产生了自己的新判断，而不是只接受了我的答案。

thinkingQuestions.title: 我会把反馈个人化，也会情绪化
thinkingQuestions.position: 下半页，反馈与代际判断之后
thinkingQuestions.original: take things personally and angry with the comments, I also emotional
thinkingQuestions.context: 前面写有“Three Voice of judgement / Cynicism / fear”和“Young people not "willing"”，后面继续写怎样接受 advice 与 feedback。
thinkingQuestions.reconstruction: 当评论触碰身份感或自尊时，我可能先把反馈理解为对我的否定，于是愤怒和防御比学习更早出现。我要先辨认情绪，再区分评论中的事实、解释和对方的立场；接受反馈不等于接受所有结论，但需要先让信息完整进入。
thinkingQuestions.evidenceBoundary: “I also emotional” 是明确的第一人称原文；情绪机制和三步区分是 Codex 的补齐，不代表原笔记已经形成该结论。
thinkingQuestions.reviewPrompt: 最近哪一句评论让我立刻想反驳？我真正捍卫的是事实、判断，还是自我形象？
thinkingQuestions.followUp: 还原一次具体反馈：原话、身体反应、第一解释、实际回应，以及 24 小时后的看法。
thinkingQuestions.learningReflection: 连续记录三次高情绪反馈，观察哪些触发器重复出现。

thinkingQuestions.title: 先听完、再总结，别替对方过早解决
thinkingQuestions.original: wait until finish -> don't interact too early / "Summary and reflection" / Only listening No clarification questions. / Still following when misunderstood / let the coachee fix his problem not provide solutions.
thinkingQuestions.context: 这是 listening / coaching 练习的连续记录，同时出现“being understand / being trusted”和会议中减少 distractions。
thinkingQuestions.reconstruction: 倾听不是等着轮到我说话，而是允许对方把意义讲完整。先听完并总结，可以检查我是否真的理解；只有在理解被确认之后，才决定需要澄清、建议还是行动。Coaching 场景里，我的责任是帮助对方拥有问题，而不是用自己的答案替代他的判断。
thinkingQuestions.evidenceBoundary: 原文是课堂练习和行为提示，不能直接证明 Leo 已经稳定做到；“只有理解确认后再决定”是整理后的原则。
thinkingQuestions.reviewPrompt: 我打断对方通常是为了效率，还是为了缓解自己不知道答案的不适？
thinkingQuestions.followUp: 下一次一对一只练习“听完 -> 总结 -> 请对方确认”，在确认前不建议。
thinkingQuestions.learningReflection: 记录对方是否补充了以前不会说出的信息，以及信任感是否发生变化。

thinkingQuestions.title: 让 Turnpo 把 sparks and ideas 变成真实成果
thinkingQuestions.original: Show your work in Turnpo < sparks and ideas come true?
thinkingQuestions.context: 这句话写在 listening/coaching 页面的最底部，明显从课堂内容跳到 Turnpo 产品或个人知识系统。
thinkingQuestions.reconstruction: Turnpo 不应只是存放最终作品，也应该让未完成的 spark 被看见、被连接、被继续加工。Show your work 的价值，是让学习过程获得反馈和下一步，使想法从私人瞬间变成可追踪的行动与产出。
thinkingQuestions.evidenceBoundary: 原文明确提出 Turnpo 与 sparks/ideas 的问题；产品机制与价值论述是 Codex 补齐，尚未由原文验证。
thinkingQuestions.reviewPrompt: 我希望 Turnpo 帮一个 spark 完成哪几个具体转化步骤？
thinkingQuestions.followUp: 选一个真实想法，记录从出现、公开、收到反馈到形成成果的全过程。
thinkingQuestions.learningReflection: 两周后检查：展示过程是否真的提高了完成率，还是只增加了记录负担。

thinkingQuestions.title: 把盲点当输入，并固定和自己约会
thinkingQuestions.original: blind spot as input / open my perspective / energized -> next? -> find what you excited and summary and do again / "diary shadowing" / appointment with me
thinkingQuestions.context: 页面从 points -> lines -> picture 的 memory-making 练习，走到 opinion/fact、perspective/truth 与反思习惯。
thinkingQuestions.reconstruction: 经验不会自动变成学习，我会把零散事件连成自己的 picture，而这个 picture 可能遗漏关键事实。盲点因此不是羞耻，而是更新解释模型的输入。固定的“appointment with me”可以让我回看什么带来能量、什么只是第一解释，并把有效做法总结后再练一次。
thinkingQuestions.evidenceBoundary: 原文中的两句“Everything...”很可能是课堂引用而非 Leo 原创；这里把它们作为触发背景，不归为个人原创观点。
thinkingQuestions.reviewPrompt: 我最近发现的一个 blind spot，究竟改变了哪一个旧判断？
thinkingQuestions.followUp: 每周预留一次 20 分钟复盘，分写 observation、interpretation、alternative、next test。
thinkingQuestions.learningReflection: 四周后检查 appointment 是否真的发生，以及哪些判断因证据而更新。

thinkingQuestions.title: True leadership：别人真正愿意跟随你
thinkingQuestions.original: Leo: "True leadership": people want to follow you ... how many people you can influence and they are willing to follow you
thinkingQuestions.context: 原句紧邻 positional、relational、process 三种 leadership perspective，后面转向 leadership 与 creativity。
thinkingQuestions.reconstruction: 我的原始判断是：真正的领导力不只来自职位，而体现在我能影响多少人，以及他们是否愿意跟随。把论述补完整，还需要追问他们愿意跟随什么方向、这种影响是否尊重自主性、最终结果是否由领导者承担。愿意跟随是重要证据，但不是领导力正当性的全部。
thinkingQuestions.evidenceBoundary: 第一句是 Leo 的明确原文；方向、伦理、自主性和责任是 Codex 为完整性加入的检验维度，不应冒充原句。
thinkingQuestions.reviewPrompt: 我认可“愿意跟随”是领导力的核心定义，还是只把它看作其中一个结果指标？
thinkingQuestions.followUp: 分别写一个因职位服从、因关系支持、因共同目标主动跟随的真实案例。
thinkingQuestions.learningReflection: 观察自己影响别人时，究竟依赖 authority、trust、clarity，还是共同创造的过程。

thinkingQuestions.title: 部门价值不能只按权力判断
thinkingQuestions.original: Topic: How do you think your department in your organization important? / How do you feel which is more important than yours and less important / "Not powerwise, the essential wise"
thinkingQuestions.context: 课堂似乎要求比较部门在组织中的重要性，笔记特别补了一句不要只从 power 看，而从 essential contribution 看。
thinkingQuestions.reconstruction: 部门的重要性不应等同于汇报层级、预算或话语权。更好的判断是：它为客户价值和组织结果承担了什么不可替代的功能，又依赖哪些其他部门共同完成。这样可以从争夺地位转向理解价值链，同时也避免把“essential”误解成某个部门天然高于其他部门。
thinkingQuestions.evidenceBoundary: “essential wise”原字可辨但英语表达不完整；价值链和相互依赖是 Codex 的补全。
thinkingQuestions.reviewPrompt: 我评价自己部门时，使用的是权力信号、资源规模，还是对整体结果的真实贡献？
thinkingQuestions.followUp: 画出一次端到端价值链，标出本部门贡献、依赖和可能被替代的部分。
thinkingQuestions.learningReflection: 与另一个部门交换视角，比较双方对“谁更重要”的叙述为什么不同。

thinkingQuestions.title: 市场在变，盲点和 bias 也会随时间变化
thinkingQuestions.original: Market changes (always find blind spot) / bias -> changed overtime
thinkingQuestions.context: 前面有电影中发现八处变化的练习、EMBA surrounding changes，以及一条字迹不完全清楚的“I see”公司复杂度观察。
thinkingQuestions.reconstruction: 盲点不是一次发现后永久消失，因为市场、组织和我的判断习惯都在移动。过去有效的解释可能随环境变化失效，因此 blind-spot review 应该是一种周期性动作：比较新信号、旧假设和实际结果，而不是只在失败后反省。
thinkingQuestions.evidenceBoundary: 页底两句清楚；公司复杂度的“I see”原句字迹不稳定，本卡不把它纳入确定结论。
thinkingQuestions.reviewPrompt: 我现在仍在使用的哪个判断，可能只是过去市场条件下的正确答案？
thinkingQuestions.followUp: 选一个重要假设，记录成立日期、支持证据、反证信号和下一次复查日期。
thinkingQuestions.learningReflection: 每月对照一次：哪些 bias 被证据修正，哪些只是换了新的合理化说法。

thinkingQuestions.kind: 课堂触发后的个人原则
thinkingQuestions.title: 让别人感到被包含：倾听、开放、不评判，也要知行合一
thinkingQuestions.original: Mirror others feel included / Listen / Not be judgemental / Open-minded / Safety / I have your back / 知行合一 - do what you do and say what you do / trust and removing fear
thinkingQuestions.context: 这些词来自 inclusion/change 练习和 psychological safety 的课堂框架，不都有 Leo 标记，但都是此前遗漏的重要手写记录。
thinkingQuestions.reconstruction: 包容不是只让每个人在场，而是让对方从我的注意、倾听和回应中感到其观点能进入讨论。不评判和 open-minded 不等于没有标准；领导者还要让承诺与行动一致，让“I have your back”成为可验证的行为，从而减少表达真实问题的恐惧。
thinkingQuestions.evidenceBoundary: 原文大部分是课堂要点，不能直接归为 Leo 已形成的原创结论；本卡是“课堂触发后的待确认原则”。
thinkingQuestions.reviewPrompt: 这些词里，哪一个真正描述了我的行为，哪一个目前只是一种愿望？
thinkingQuestions.followUp: 请一位同事举例说明：什么时候他感到被我听见，什么时候没有。
thinkingQuestions.learningReflection: 用可观察行为复盘 safety，而不是只用“团队气氛不错”来判断。

thinkingQuestions.title: 组织不同层级关注不同问题
thinkingQuestions.original: I see: Different layers focus. / C-level, mid-management, execution layer / learning culture
thinkingQuestions.context: 页面随后记录 left-hand column、listener perspective、on-the-job learning、Nonaka Takeuchi 和 70/20/10。
thinkingQuestions.reconstruction: 我看到组织不同层级拥有不同的注意对象：高层更关注方向和资源，中层负责翻译与协调，执行层面对具体任务和反馈。学习文化不能只给所有人同一套信息，而要让知识在层级之间被翻译、反馈和重新组合，否则战略与现场会彼此失真。
thinkingQuestions.evidenceBoundary: “Different layers focus”是明确 I see 原文；各层具体关注内容与知识翻译是 Codex 补齐，需要 Leo 用实际组织经验验证。
thinkingQuestions.reviewPrompt: Turnpo 当前最严重的层级信息断点发生在哪里？
thinkingQuestions.followUp: 选一个决策，分别写出高层、中层、执行层看见的问题和缺失的信息。
thinkingQuestions.learningReflection: 检查一次跨层沟通后，执行反馈是否真正回到了决策层。

thinkingQuestions.title: Knowledge and insight need a home
thinkingQuestions.original: Make sure knowledge and insight get a "home" in your organisation / Allocate reflection time / be a storyteller, sparring partner or mentor / build communities of practice
thinkingQuestions.context: 这组课堂笔记之后立刻进入 AI use、generated content、mastery test 和个人 AI 思考。
thinkingQuestions.reconstruction: 洞察如果只留在个人脑中，就不会成为组织能力。给知识一个 home，不只是建文件夹，而是明确谁维护、何时复用、如何验证、怎样在 community of practice 中继续修正。反思时间、故事、mentor 和 sparring partner 都是让隐性经验转成共享能力的机制。
thinkingQuestions.evidenceBoundary: 原文是课堂要点；维护责任、复用和验证机制是 Codex 对“home”的操作化补充。
thinkingQuestions.reviewPrompt: 目前哪一类关键知识离开某个人就会消失？
thinkingQuestions.followUp: 选一个高价值经验，指定 home、owner、检索词、复用场景和 review date。
thinkingQuestions.learningReflection: 一个月后检查它是否被别人独立找到并使用，而不是只被存档。

thinkingQuestions.title: AI 应提高上限，但 human in the lead
thinkingQuestions.original: Leo: How to define AI usage. / 60 -> 80 normal. / 80 -> 120 with AI / Not let AI guide or generate all / human in the lead
thinkingQuestions.context: 前面写有“Not -> content copy from "generate content"”和“What you learn speak up and test”。
thinkingQuestions.reconstruction: AI 的价值不应只按使用次数衡量，而应看它是否提高了分析、比较、表达和验证的上限。60、80、120 更像一种能力隐喻：人先拥有基本理解和判断，AI 再放大，而不是用漂亮输出掩盖认知空缺。Human in the lead 意味着人定义问题、提供语境、核查事实、做取舍并承担结果。
thinkingQuestions.evidenceBoundary: 数字含义没有在原文中被正式定义；“能力隐喻”和五项 human ownership 是 Codex 的解释，不是课堂已确认标准。
thinkingQuestions.reviewPrompt: 我是否同意 60/80/120 的这个解释？每一档在我的工作里可观察的标准是什么？
thinkingQuestions.followUp: 选择一个真实任务，分别记录无 AI、AI 辅助和最终人工判断的差异。
thinkingQuestions.learningReflection: 复盘 AI 提高的是质量、速度还是只提高了表面完成度。

thinkingQuestions.title: 有 AI 以后，怎样测试真正掌握知识
thinkingQuestions.position: 页面下半部，问号与 I see 标记
thinkingQuestions.original: How to test in the future / I see: Same as qualification test how people master the knowledge / How the future assessment
thinkingQuestions.context: 问题紧接 human in the lead，说明注意力从“能否生成”转向“人是否真正掌握”。
thinkingQuestions.reconstruction: 当答案可以即时生成，assessment 不应只检查最终文本，而要检查一个人能否解释理由、识别错误、迁移到新情境并在质疑下修正。AI 可以参与过程，但掌握度必须通过人的现场判断和应用表现被看见。
thinkingQuestions.evidenceBoundary: 原文提出问题并类比 qualification test；解释、迁移、纠错和现场应用是 Codex 建议的测试维度。
thinkingQuestions.reviewPrompt: 对我自己的 EMBA 学习，哪一种测试最能区分“看过答案”和“真正掌握”？
thinkingQuestions.followUp: 为一个本月概念设计四项测试：不用资料解释、找反例、迁移案例、行动复盘。
thinkingQuestions.learningReflection: 一个月后重复测试，观察知识是否仍能被独立调用。

thinkingQuestions.title: 01｜保留判断：让 AI 总结我的思考，而不是替我产生立场
thinkingQuestions.original: "Use AI summarize my thought." / Business input -> Prompt for generating / thinking logic
thinkingQuestions.context: 这是 AI mastery discussion 后的个人工作流草图；原文不是“I see”，此前转录曾误标。
thinkingQuestions.reconstruction: 更合适的顺序是先由我提供真实业务输入和初步判断，再让 AI 帮我整理逻辑、发现缺口或形成可继续追问的 prompt。这样 AI 放大的是我的思考过程，而不是用通用答案替代我的立场。最终版本仍要标明我接受、修改或拒绝了什么。
thinkingQuestions.evidenceBoundary: 原文明确写“summarize my thought”；发现缺口与最终判断记录是 Codex 补充的防失真机制。
thinkingQuestions.reviewPrompt: 我实际使用 AI 时，通常是先有自己的 thought，还是先让 AI 给我一个看似完整的答案？
thinkingQuestions.followUp: 用同一问题比较两条流程：AI-first 与 Leo-thought-first，并保存差异。
thinkingQuestions.learningReflection: 判断哪条流程更能保留个人观点、业务细节和可解释性。

thinkingQuestions.title: 02｜留下过程：Learning is the process; working is the result
thinkingQuestions.position: 页面上半部，方框与 Leo 箭头
thinkingQuestions.original: Learning is the process / Working is the Result -> Leo
thinkingQuestions.context: 页面主题是 storytelling 与和真实人物互动，随后进入演讲、目标听众和视觉故事。
thinkingQuestions.reconstruction: 工作通常只暴露结果，但学习发生在形成结果的过程里：尝试、反馈、修正和再次实践。如果组织只评价结果，就可能丢掉可复用的方法；如果只谈学习而没有结果，又容易变成 fake effort。完整闭环应同时保留过程证据和结果检验。
thinkingQuestions.evidenceBoundary: 原文只有两行对比；组织评价、fake effort 与闭环是 Codex 结合 Leo 既有关注补齐。
thinkingQuestions.reviewPrompt: 我想表达的是“学习与工作不同”，还是“工作结果必须保留可见的学习过程”？
thinkingQuestions.followUp: 选一个完成的项目，补写关键试错、判断变化和可复用方法。
thinkingQuestions.learningReflection: 检查这些过程记录能否帮助另一个人更快完成类似工作。

thinkingQuestions.title: 03｜共同取舍：资源有限时，冲突不是偶然
thinkingQuestions.position: 页面下半部，Leo thinking 箭头
thinkingQuestions.original: Resource if limited, the battle will happen -> Leo thinking
thinkingQuestions.context: 这句话位于 presentation practice 与 story structure 之间，原页没有继续解释 battle 指什么。
thinkingQuestions.reconstruction: 当资源稀缺而目标、优先级和分配规则又不清楚时，冲突会成为结构性结果，而不只是某个人难合作。领导者需要把稀缺说清楚，建立取舍标准和升级机制，同时检查所谓“battle”是否也被权力不对称或信息不透明放大。
thinkingQuestions.evidenceBoundary: 原文只确认“资源有限会发生 battle”；成因和领导动作是 Codex 补齐，不能当成 Leo 已明确写出的论证。
thinkingQuestions.reviewPrompt: 我当时想到的是哪一种资源、哪一场 battle？
thinkingQuestions.followUp: 补回原始案例，并区分真实稀缺、优先级冲突、角色不清和沟通失败。
thinkingQuestions.learningReflection: 下一次资源争议后复盘：规则是否让冲突更可解释、更公平、更快解决。

thinkingQuestions.title: 04｜推动理解：先确定听众，再用 Who? Why? How? -> What 组织故事
thinkingQuestions.position: IMG_6910 中下部；IMG_6911 中下部
thinkingQuestions.original: Target Audience / What information you want share / Who? Why? How? -> What / Make it personal / keep it Authentic / Target the Audience / Stickiness / personal feeling more / emotion with the story
thinkingQuestions.context: storytelling 被写成 interactive；随后用 1997 China、3rd line city、7 yrs old 的个人经历把城市变化转成故事。
thinkingQuestions.reconstruction: 表达不应从“我有什么内容”开始，而应从“这个听众需要理解和记住什么”开始。Who、Why、How 帮助建立人物、意义和过程，最后的 What 才落到信息或行动。Personal 和 authentic 不是装饰，而是用真实经历让抽象数据进入记忆，但故事仍必须忠于事实。
thinkingQuestions.evidenceBoundary: 结构原文是“Who? Why? How? -> What”，此前曾被误转成 What 开头；关于事实忠实是 Codex 补充的边界。
thinkingQuestions.reviewPrompt: 这个顺序是否符合我当时的意思？最后一个 What 指结论、行动，还是故事对象？
thinkingQuestions.followUp: 用 1997 China 的真实经历写一个 90 秒版本，并逐项核对事实与听众目标。
thinkingQuestions.learningReflection: 测试听众 24 小时后记住了什么，以及记住的是观点还是只有情绪。

thinkingQuestions.title: 05｜校正判断：从 autopilot 到 focus 的第二次观察
thinkingQuestions.original: Where you home. current? / Communication / 1st feeling Autopilot -> / 2st feeling focus / The culture MAP / different form
thinkingQuestions.context: 这是当天最后一页，内容很短，像是 inclusion/culture exercise 的提示词，没有写出具体案例和结论。
thinkingQuestions.reconstruction: 跨文化沟通中，第一感觉常由既有经验自动生成；第二次更专注的观察，才可能看见对方当前的归属、语境和表达方式。Culture Map 可以提供假设，但不能把个人简化成国家标签，因此需要用提问和真实互动校正。
thinkingQuestions.evidenceBoundary: 本页原文碎片化，完整论述主要是 Codex 的谨慎补全；“不能简化成国家标签”不是原句。
thinkingQuestions.reviewPrompt: “1st feeling / 2st feeling”当时具体指哪一个课堂练习和哪一次感受？
thinkingQuestions.followUp: 补写练习对象、第一反应、第二次观察以及 Culture Map 改变了什么。
thinkingQuestions.learningReflection: 在下一次跨文化对话中记录第一判断，并用一个问题主动寻找反证。

followUpPoints: [T01] 补回一个真实 personal struggle 的完整事件，而不是只保留课堂题目。
[T03] 还原一次让我愤怒或防御的反馈，区分原话、情绪、解释和回应。
[T04] 用一个实际对话验证“先听完再总结”是否带来更多信息与信任。
[T07] 由 Leo 确认 True leadership 的定义，并决定是否加入方向、伦理、结果与责任。
[T08] 用真实价值链检验部门的 essential contribution，而不是停留在权力比较。
[T13-T15] 定义 60 / 80 / 120、human in the lead、mastery test 和 AI-first / thought-first 的标准。
[T16] 明确 learning process 与 working result 的关系，并补一个真实项目。
[T17] 补回 resource limited 对应的具体资源和 battle。
[T18] 确认 Who? Why? How? -> What 的含义，并完成 1997 China 的 90 秒故事。
[T19] 补写 Inclusion & Diversity 练习中的第一感觉、第二次观察和 Culture Map 作用。
[待核原字] 回看 IMG_6906 的公司复杂度句、IMG_6910 的 speech 前置词、IMG_6911 的 Gender/Leader 词。
[行动闭环] 每条确认保留的 insight 增加 baseline、行为实验、成功信号和 review date。

months.reflection: September 2026 is the first core finance week. The learning goal is financial leadership: connect investment and financing choices, accounting information, performance control, enterprise risk, compliance and ESG reporting into one decision framework. The priority is not memorising isolated models, but using them to diagnose a real company and make a well-supported recommendation.
months.markdown:
# Corporate Finance and Accounting - September 2026

## Course week

7-11 September 2026. The module covers Financial Management, Compliance, Sustainability Reporting, Financial Accounting and Analysis, Enterprise Risk Management, and Management Accounting and Control.

## What I need to master

1. Make investment, financing and risk decisions using risk-return, discounting and downside-protection logic.
2. Read financial statements and use accounting information, ratios and KPIs for decisions.
3. Design management controls that support strategy without creating false precision or harmful incentives.
4. Apply COSO ERM: governance and culture, strategy/objectives, performance, review/revision, and information/reporting.
5. Diagnose compliance failure through controls, culture, accountability, data and escalation.
6. Assess sustainability reporting through double materiality, IROs, value-chain coverage, metrics, targets and assurance.

## Assessment focus

The individual final assignment is a real-life integrated case. Content and application carry 75%; critical reflection on choices, assumptions, limitations and AI use carries 15%; form, concise writing and APA references carry 10%. Use the study cards to turn each reading into evidence for a recommendation, rather than a standalone summary.
